parole.significato: A person who rows a caique.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French caïquejee, ultimately from Turkish kayıkçı (“boatman”).

parole.significato: Any of certain wild canids of the genera Lupulella and Canis, native to the tropical Old World and smaller than a wolf.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French chacal, chacale, checale, schakal, ciacale, from Turkish çakal, from Ottoman Turkish چقال (çakâl), from Classical Persian شغال (šaġāl), borrowed from Sanskrit शृगाल (śṛgāla, “jackal”), the alternative form of सृगाल (sṛgāla).

parole.significato: A large Oriental tobacco pipe wherein the smoke is drawn through water to filter and cool it.
parole.testo: From French narghilé, from Turkish nargile, from Persian نارگیله (nârgile) from نارگیل (nârgil, “a coconut”), which was formerly used to construct the bowl, likely ultimately from Sanskrit नारिकेल (nārikela, “a coconut”), from a Dravidian language.
